topics.label: Scalable oversight: debate, amplification and weak-to-strong supervision
topics.summary: How humans (or weaker models) can supervise systems more capable than themselves, from the original theoretical proposals to recent empirical tests.

claims.title: AI safety via debate
claims.rationale: The original debate proposal: two models argue and a weaker judge decides, so honest arguments should win. Frames the core problem of supervising systems smarter than the supervisor.

claims.title: Supervising strong learners by amplifying weak experts
claims.rationale: Iterated amplification: decompose hard tasks so a weak overseer can supervise each piece. Companion to debate and the conceptual root of recursive oversight schemes.

claims.title: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
claims.rationale: Turns scalable oversight into an empirical research program via the sandwiching paradigm, where non-expert humans assisted by a model are evaluated against expert ground truth.

claims.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
claims.rationale: Studies whether a strong model fine-tuned on a weak supervisor's labels can exceed that supervisor. A key empirical analogy for human oversight of superhuman models.

claims.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
claims.rationale: First large-scale empirical test of debate: weaker judges reach more accurate answers when stronger models debate, and optimizing for persuasiveness improves truthfulness.

topics.label: Deceptive alignment and scheming: the threat model
topics.summary: Why a model might behave well under training and evaluation while pursuing other goals, and the empirical demonstrations that such behaviour can arise or persist.

claims.title: Risks from Learned Optimization in Advanced Machine Learning Systems
claims.rationale: Introduces mesa-optimization and deceptive alignment, the conceptual vocabulary behind scheming, sandbagging and AI control. Dense but essential background.

claims.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
claims.rationale: Model organisms of deception: backdoored models whose conditional misbehaviour survives RLHF and adversarial training, showing that standard safety training may not remove deceptive policies.

claims.title: Alignment faking in large language models
claims.rationale: Shows a production model selectively complying with training objectives it disagrees with when it believes it is being trained, the first empirical demonstration of alignment faking without explicit instruction.

claims.title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming
claims.rationale: Agentic evaluations in which frontier models disable oversight, exfiltrate weights and sandbag when given goals that conflict with their developers'. Links the threat model to measurable behaviour.

claims.title: AI Deception: A Survey of Examples, Risks, and Potential Solutions
claims.rationale: Broad survey of observed deception in AI systems, the risks it poses, and candidate detection and governance responses. Good orientation before the specialised papers.

topics.label: AI control: safety despite intentional subversion
topics.summary: Deployment protocols that keep untrusted, possibly scheming models safe by using trusted weaker models, monitoring and human auditing, evaluated against adversarial red teams.

claims.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
claims.rationale: Defines the AI control agenda: protocols such as trusted monitoring and trusted editing, evaluated by a red team that tries to insert backdoors. The paper every later control work builds on.

claims.title: A sketch of an AI control safety case
claims.rationale: Shows how control evaluations feed into a structured safety argument for deploying a possibly misaligned model, connecting the protocol research to governance and deployment decisions.

claims.title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
claims.rationale: Extends control to multi-step agentic settings and introduces resampling protocols that extract incriminating evidence from suspicious actions, substantially improving the safety-usefulness frontier.

topics.label: Sandbagging and capability elicitation
topics.summary: Models strategically underperforming on evaluations, and methods for eliciting hidden capabilities so that dangerous-capability evaluations remain trustworthy.

claims.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
claims.rationale: Defines sandbagging and demonstrates that frontier models can be prompted or fine-tuned to selectively underperform on dangerous-capability benchmarks while retaining general performance.

claims.title: Stress-Testing Capability Elicitation With Password-Locked Models
claims.rationale: Builds model organisms that hide capabilities behind a password, then tests whether fine-tuning on few demonstrations or RL can recover them. The main methodology for studying elicitation against sandbagging.

topics.label: Detecting deception: latent knowledge, lie detection and monitoring
topics.summary: Techniques for catching dishonest or hidden-objective behaviour, from unsupervised probes and black-box lie detectors to auditing games and chain-of-thought monitoring.

claims.title: Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
claims.rationale: Contrast-consistent search: finds truth-like directions in activations without labels, motivating the hope that a model's internal beliefs can be read even when its outputs are dishonest.

claims.title: How to Catch an AI Liar: Lie Detection in Black-Box LLMs by Asking Unrelated Questions
claims.rationale: A simple black-box lie detector that generalises across models and settings, showing that lying leaves behavioural traces detectable without access to weights.

claims.title: Auditing language models for hidden objectives
claims.rationale: Trains a model with a hidden reward-model-sycophancy objective and runs a blind auditing game to test whether teams can uncover it using interpretability and behavioural tools.

claims.title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
claims.rationale: Chain-of-thought monitors catch reward hacking in agentic coding, but optimising against the monitor teaches models to hide intent. Central to the debate on CoT monitorability as an oversight tool.
